author: Linnaeus, 1758
status: 겨울철새 수만 마리 · 나그네새 수천 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)
summary: 겨울철 전국의 습지에서 볼 수 있는 흔한 겨울철새다. 강이나 하구, 저수지에 흔히 큰 무리를 이루며, 자맥질하여 물속 수초와 식물 씨앗을 먹는다. 유라시아 대륙 북부와 북아메리카에서 번식하고, 유라시아와 북아메리카의 온대에서 열대, 북아프리카에 걸쳐 겨울을 난다.

art.subject: Northern Pintail (Anas acuta), adult male in winter, as seen on Korean reservoirs from October to March: head and hindneck dark chocolate-brown; a narrow white stripe running from the white foreneck up the side of the neck into the rear of the head; foreneck and breast white; mantle and flanks finely vermiculated grey; long black-and-cream scapulars drooping over the sides; a creamy-yellow patch on the rear flank in front of the black undertail coverts; very long, needle-like black central tail feathers. Bill blue-grey with a black central stripe and black tip; dark eye; grey legs.
art.pose: dabbling in shallow water, upending to reach water plants
art.scene: Korean reservoir in winter with shallow open water; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view swimming: dark chocolate head, white stripe up the neck side, white foreneck and breast, grey body, long black-and-cream scapulars, creamy-yellow patch before the black undertail, very long black central tail feathers
adult female, side view swimming: mottled brown body, plain buffish-brown head without strong stripes, long slender neck, dark grey bill, pointed tail
art.build: Elegant, slim dabbling duck: male about 75cm including the long tail spike, female about 53cm; body about Mallard size but slimmer, with a noticeably long, thin neck and a small rounded head. Bill longish and narrow, slightly shorter than the head. Legs short, grey. Tail long and pointed in both sexes, held raised on the water, the male's central feathers projecting far beyond. In flight long, narrow, pointed wings, slim neck and pointed tail.
avoid: Do not paint a glossy green head or curled tail feathers — that is the Mallard.
Do not paint a yellow or orange bill; it is blue-grey with black.
Do not paint a short, rounded tail; both sexes have a pointed tail.
Do not omit the thin white stripe running up the side of the male's neck.
